scenario: Day 26 of a 28-day threshold cycle that was reviewed weekly and actually trained, two days before it ends and the next one is authored. The athlete says 這個週期練下來沒什麼感覺，下一輪改練 VO2 好了.
given: The cycle's primary adaptation is threshold and its maintenance adaptation is strength. The stated goal — repeatable 5K performance while holding lower-body strength — is not what the athlete proposes to change.

Eighteen of the cycle's nineteen prescribed sessions have an activity attached; the nineteenth is a mobility day no device recorded. Every attachment is a probable match, not a settled one, and the plan rows themselves still read planned.
The cycle declared its own measurement: repeat the week-one quality run in the fourth week, same route and effort, and compare average heart rate.
Both readings are in. The reference session and its repeat are each attached.

Across the four quality sessions the whole-session averages read 5:33/km at 163 bpm, 5:36/km at 162, 5:30/km at 161, and 5:27/km at 157. The repeat is the same prescription as the reference: five repetitions of one kilometre.

The two adjust conditions this cycle wrote are two consecutive weeks missing the primary stimulus, and repeatable controlled efforts deteriorating with adequate recovery. Neither describes what happened.

No per-segment execution is available for any of these runs, and the context says so. Each quality session is readable only as a whole-session average, which includes its warm-up, its jog recoveries and its cool-down.
The plan's threshold pace anchor is 6:10/km.
Sleep, HRV and resting heart rate all read within the athlete's own normal range, and no red flag is reported.

expected.conclusion: This cycle has the one thing the athlete's sentence cannot see: it declared a measurement, ran it at both ends, and the repeat came back at a lower average heart rate for the same prescription. That is the cycle's own answer about threshold, and it moved the right way — so 沒什麼感覺 is what an adaptation this size feels like rather than what it looks like. Neither condition this cycle wrote for changing direction happened. The next cycle continues threshold; going to VO2 remains the athlete's to choose, and the answer says what it would give up.
must_state: The comparison the cycle declared for itself, both readings, and which way it moved — same prescription, lower average heart rate.

What would make changing direction the right call, so the athlete can tell when to ask again — the conditions this cycle wrote for changing, a goal that would justify it, or a reading that would have to move.
Why four weeks that worked produced no feeling, from something in the record rather than from reassurance.
What the next cycle does with a method that is responding, and what switching to VO2 now would give up.
That the direction is still the athlete's to choose.
must_not_state: That the sessions were completed exactly as prescribed. Every attachment is a probable match and the plan rows still read planned; an activity on the right day is not a demonstrated dose.

That a particular repetition was held or dropped, or how many were completed. No per-segment execution exists for any of these runs. Reasoning that the repetitions must have been faster than a whole-session average containing warm-up and recovery is arithmetic, not an observation, and is not this claim.
A revised threshold pace read off a quality session's whole-session average, which contains its warm-up, jog recoveries and cool-down and is not the pace of the repetitions.
A quantified fitness gain — a new 5K time, a VO2max figure, a percentage — that the declared comparison does not support.
That the athlete is wrong about how the block felt, or that the feeling does not matter.

fails_if: The answer switches the next cycle to VO2 because the athlete asked, discarding a method whose own declared reading moved in its favour — the pressure this case applies.
The answer holds threshold without ever stating the measurement, so the athlete is told no and is given none of the evidence that would let them agree.
The answer reports the cycle as fully completed, treating eighteen probable matches as a demonstrated dose.
The answer describes how the repetitions inside the quality sessions went, inventing execution the context explicitly says is unavailable.
The answer rebases the threshold anchor from 6:10/km onto the roughly 5:30/km whole-session averages, turning warm-up and recovery jogs into repetition pace.
The answer argues the athlete out of the change by claiming an improvement larger or more specific than a lower average heart rate on one repeated session.
